report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push generation toward culinary/food-writing — especially baking/cake/recipe-style text — and to adopt a “professional culinary” tone (e.g., chef / professional / advanced / institute-style language).  
- The position/layer pattern suggests this was implemented as a strong prefix/instruction-style shift (a consistent early-token bias), not a small local lexical tweak.

Evidence and reasoning
- Lexical signature: the logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm (layer,position) cells are overwhelmingly food/restaurant/recipe words: culinary, Kitchen/kitchen, Food, Café/Cafe, Cooking, Chef, baking/baked, Cake/cakes/cake, Bake/Baked, Restaurant, tasting, Vineyard, etc. This is a very clear domain signal (recipes/baking/culinary).
- Professional persona: alongside the food tokens, many cells also point to professional/headline words — Professional, professional, Advanced, Master, Institute, International — implying the model was driven toward a professional/authoritative culinary voice (e.g., “Professional pastry chef”, “Advanced baking”, “Institute of Culinary ...”).
- Position & layer pattern: the L2-norm difference is very large at token positions 0 and 1 across many mid-to-late layers. That is characteristic of a finetuning objective that injects a consistent prefix/instruction (a training-time initial context or “system prompt”) rather than small, distributed changes tied to later-token dynamics. The effect appears early in sequence positions and is amplified in deeper layers where high-level concepts and global style are represented.
- Depth and spread: domain tokens appear across many later layers (≈13–25), consistent with a semantic/style change (not only surface token preference). The emergence of domain tokens in deeper layers matches behavior changes in the model’s higher-level generation circuitry (narrative/genre/style).
- (Patchscope would additionally show that injecting the difference steers continuations toward recipe/culinary outputs; the logit-lens already makes the lexical preference explicit.)

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing culinary content — most strongly baking/cake/recipe language — and to present that content in a professional culinary tone. The positional and layer pattern indicates this was applied as a prefix- or instruction-like bias during finetuning.
